newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Roche, Agouron in marketing pact.
newsitem.headline: Roche, Agouron in marketing pact.

text.p: Roche Holding AG said it concluded a marketing agreement with Agouron Pharmaceuticals Inc of the U.S. covering Viracept, an anti-HIV drug co-developed by Agouron and Japan Tobacco Inc.

Terms of the agreement call for Roche to receive exclusive marketing rights for Viracept in Europe and other countries while Agouron retains the rights in North America and Japan Tobacco the rights for Asia.
Roche said it will pay Agouron and Japan Tobacco $9 million each upon signing the agreement and an additional $11 million to each of the two companies when Viracept is first approved in Europe.
Thereafter, Roche will pay Agouron and Japan Tobacco a royalty based on Roche's sales of Viracept.
Viracept is a synthetic chemical compound designed to inhibit HIV protease enzyme. This enzyme plans an important role in the replication of HIV.

Current data suggest that Viracept, together with the Roche protease inhibitor Invirase, may prove to be a good anti-HIV therapy because of the two drugs' resistance and cross resistance profiles, Roche said in its statement.

Agouron filed a New Drug Application for Viracept with the U.S. Food and Drug Administration in December 1996 and it expects to file marketing applications in major European countries later this year.
